title: Time-dependent integrable quantum field theories with dynamical boundaries
abstract: We present a method for constructing time-dependent integrable chiral quantum field theories on a finite spatial interval from the scattering and reflection data of an autonomous integrable model. Each particle carries a spectral label that is constant along its free trajectory. Requiring a right--left scattering event at a fixed time to be independent of its position forces the map from characteristic coordinates to spectral labels to be affine, with the same slope for both chiralities. As a result, all bulk scattering events at a given time sample one common spectral argument, and the two boundary reflections sample the corresponding endpoint arguments. The bulk and boundary drives are not independent time-dependent deformations: their time dependence is fixed by the same affine spectral coordinate. Successive reflections at the two endpoints translate the spectral label by a finite amount. Following a particle through a complete round trip then produces a difference transport whose consistency gives the boundary quantum Knizhnik--Zamolodchikov equations. The Yang--Baxter and reflection equations ensure local compatibility, while BqKZ flatness ensures compatibility of complete round trips. We then reconstruct the local Hamiltonian by inverting the one- and two-particle matching problems. The bulk matrix fixes the contact interaction, while the reflection matrix fixes the corresponding boundary coupling. The same autonomous factorized data determine the boundary qKZ transport problem and the local driven Hamiltonian. Once the boundary qKZ system is solved, its characteristic pullback gives the corresponding time-dependent many-body wavefunction. We illustrate the construction with rational $SU(N)$ models and an $O(3)$-invariant model with dynamical boundary impurities, obtaining driven Kondo interactions whose couplings are fixed by the same affine spectral coordinate.
summary: This work constructs time-dependent integrable quantum field theories on a finite interval by demanding consistency between bulk scattering and boundary reflections. The core finding is that the time dependence is governed by a single affine spectral coordinate, leading to the boundary quantum Knizhnik-Zamolodchikov equations. This provides a powerful, mathematically rigorous tool for modeling driven quantum systems with boundaries.
main_problem: The paper develops a method to construct time-dependent integrable chiral quantum field theories defined on a finite spatial interval with dynamical boundaries.
main_result: The time dependence of the bulk and boundary drives is constrained by a single common affine spectral coordinate, leading to the boundary quantum Knizhnik-Zamolodchikov (BqKZ) equations.
method: The construction relies on matching conditions derived from scattering and reflection data, ensuring consistency via the Yang-Baxter and reflection equations.
model_or_system: The system involves chiral quantum fields ($\psi_R, \psi_L$) on a finite interval $[0, L]$, incorporating time-dependent bulk and boundary interactions, exemplified by rational SU(N) and O(3) impurity models.
key_observables: The time-dependent many-body wavefunction, the boundary coupling, and the spectral labels carried by particles.
important_parameters: The drive rate $\kappa$, the boundary length $L$, and the spectral labels $\zeta_R, \zeta_L$.
main_assumptions: The theory assumes the existence of an underlying autonomous integrable model whose scattering/reflection data dictates the time evolution, and that the map from free trajectories to spectral labels is affine.
paper_structure: The paper proceeds by establishing the affine structure of spectral labels from free propagation, enforcing consistency via the Yang-Baxter and reflection equations, deriving the BqKZ equations from round-trip consistency, and finally reconstructing the local Hamiltonian from matching problems.
why_interesting: The rigorous mathematical framework connecting integrable field theory structures (like QKZ/BqKZ) to time-dependent boundary dynamics is highly relevant for understanding open quantum systems where boundary effects or impurities drive the dynamics.
